newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Wave of political tension hits Indonesia's Java.
newsitem.headline: Wave of political tension hits Indonesia's Java.

text.p: A wave of political violence hit Indonesia's Central Java province over the weekend, just days before campaigning officially begins for May general elections, news reports and residents said.

The Jakarta Post newspaper on Monday quoted sources as saying one person was injured in a village in Temanggung regency, south of the provincial capital Semarang, in a fight on Saturday between villagers and supporters of the Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP).

In nearby Pekalongan regency, residents said two people were injured when about 300 PPP supporters attacked the office of the assistant regent on Sunday. The reason for the attack was not immediately clear.
Local government officials said the incidents were minor and police said the situation was calm and under control.
Residents said a motorcycle convoy of hundreds of PPP supporters in Batang regency, between Pekalongan and Semarang, tore down and burned flags of the ruling Golkar party on Saturday afternoon.
They said the act was in retaliation for an attack on a group of PPP supporters by a stone-throwing mob from a Golkar-affiliated youth group the day before.

Meanwhile, residents in Yogyakarta said riot police were posted on key arterial roads out of the central Java city as hundreds of supporters of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) took to the streets in a convoy.
Street parades and convoys are banned during the official 27-day campaign period which begins on Sunday.

There have been several clashes in central Java between supporters of the three sanctioned political parties as jockeying intensifies in the country's most populous province in the lead-up to the May 29 poll.
The election campaign begins on Sunday. The government lets only the ruling Golkar, the PPP and the Christian-Nationalist Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) contest elections.

Meanwhile, an Indonesian court has convicted 21 people and acquitted five in connection with ethnic and religious rioting last January in the West Java town of Rengasdengklok, the official Antara news agency said on Monday.
It said the Karawang State Court on Saturday handed down sentences of between two and four months jail for the people convicted.
Earlier this month, an Indonesian man of Chinese descent was jailed for three years and six months for provoking the riot in Rengasdengklok, 50 km (30 miles) east of Jakarta, on January 30.
The court was told the man scolded Moslem youths who were beating drums before dawn to summon people to eat before the start of daytime Moslem fasting during Ramadan.
A mainly Moslem mob later attacked churches and Chinese temples, looted homes and shops and burned 16 cars.
